=== sync-vendor head ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
VENDOR_YAML="$REPO_ROOT/vendor.yaml"
VENDOR_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/skills/vendor"

# Colors
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") [OPTIONS] [SKILL_NAME]

Sync vendored skills from upstream repositories.

Options:
  --check    Dry-run: check for upstream updates without syncing
  -h, --help Show this help message

Arguments:
  SKILL_NAME  Optional: sync only the named skill (default: sync all)

Entries with a top-level `frozen:` block in vendor.yaml are skipped (the
vendored copy is kept as-is). Use this when an upstream skill is deleted or
renamed away but you want to keep shipping the last-synced version.

Dependencies: gh (GitHub CLI), yq (YAML processor)
EOF
}

check_deps() {
  local missing=()
  command -v gh &>/dev/null || missing+=(gh)
  command -v yq &>/dev/null || missing+=(yq)
  if [[ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    echo -e "${RED}Error: Missing dependencies: ${missing[*]}${NC}" >&2
    if [[ "$(uname -s)" == "Darwin" ]]; then
      echo "  macOS:  brew install ${missing[*]}" >&2
    else
      echo "  Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt install ${missing[*]}" >&2
      echo "  Fedora/RHEL:   sudo dnf install ${missing[*]}" >&2
      echo "  Arch:          sudo pacman -S ${missing[*]}" >&2
      echo "  Or via: snap install ${missing[*]}" >&2
    fi
    exit 1
  fi
  # Check gh auth
  if ! gh auth status &>/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo -e "${RED}Error: gh is not authenticated. Run 'gh auth login' first.${NC}" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

# Get the number of skills in vendor.yaml
skill_count() {
  yq '.skills | length' "$VENDOR_YAML"
}

# Get a field from a skill entry by index
skill_field() {
  local idx="$1" field="$2"
  yq ".skills[$idx].$field" "$VENDOR_YAML"
}

# Get latest commit SHA for a path in a repo (path="." means repo root)
get_latest_commit() {
  local owner="$1" repo="$2" branch="$3" path="$4"
  if [[ "$path" == "." ]]; then
    gh api "repos/$owner/$repo/commits?sha=$branch&per_page=1" \
      --jq '.[0].sha' 2>/dev/null || echo ""
  else
    gh api "repos/$owner/$repo/commits?sha=$branch&path=$path&per_page=1" \
      --jq '.[0].sha' 2>/dev/null || echo ""
  fi
}

```text
# Get the blob SHA for one file, used to detect license-only updates without
# treating every unrelated commit in a large upstream repo as a skill update.
get_file_sha() {
  local owner="$1" repo="$2" branch="$3" path="$4"
  gh api "repos/$owner/$repo/contents/$path?ref=$branch" \
    --jq '.sha' 2>/dev/null || echo ""
}

download_file() {
  local owner="$1" repo="$2" branch="$3" src_path="$4" dest_path="$5"
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest_path")"
  gh api "repos/$owner/$repo/contents/$src_path?ref=$branch" \
    --jq '.content' | base64 -d > "$dest_path"
}

# Download a directory tree from GitHub. src_path="." means whole repo root.
download_tree() {
  local owner="$1" repo="$2" branch="$3" src_path="$4" dest_dir="$5"

  mkdir -p "$dest_dir"

  # Get directory contents recursively using git trees API
  local tree_sha
  if [[ "$src_path" == "." ]]; then
    tree_sha=$(gh api "repos/$owner/$repo/git/trees/$branch?recursive=1" \
      --jq '.tree[] | .path + "\t" + .type + "\t" + (.url // "")')
  else
    tree_sha=$(gh api "repos/$owner/$repo/git/trees/$branch?recursive=1" \
      --jq '.tree[] | select(.path | startswith("'"$src_path"'/")) | .path + "\t" + .type + "\t" + (.url // "")')
  fi

  if [[ -z "$tree_sha" ]]; then
    echo -e "${RED}Error: No files found at $owner/$repo/$src_path${NC}" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  # Process each file
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r file_path file_type file_url; do
    local rel_path
    if [[ "$src_path" == "." ]]; then
      rel_path="$file_path"
    else
      rel_path="${file_path#"$src_path"/}"
    fi
    local dest_path="$dest_dir/$rel_path"

    if [[ "$file_type" == "tree" ]]; then
      mkdir -p "$dest_path"
    elif [[ "$file_type" == "blob" ]]; then
      mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest_path")"
      # Download file content via the blob API
      gh api "$file_url" --jq '.content' | base64 -d > "$dest_path"
    fi
  done <<< "$tree_sha"
}

sync_skill() {
  local idx="$1" check_only="${2:-false}"

  local name series owner repo path branch license_path last_commit last_license_sha
  name=$(skill_field "$idx" "name")
  series=$(skill_field "$idx" "series")
  owner=$(skill_field "$idx" "upstream.owner")
  repo=$(skill_field "$idx" "upstream.repo")
  path=$(skill_field "$idx" "upstream.path")
  branch=$(skill_field "$idx" "upstream.branch")
  license_path=$(skill_field "$idx" "license_path")
  last_commit=$(skill_field "$idx" "last_sync.commit")
  last_license_sha=$(skill_field "$idx" "last_sync.license_sha")

  # Normalize yq null to empty
  [[ "$last_commit" == "null" || "$last_commit" == '""' ]] && last_commit=""
  [[ "$last_license_sha" == "null" || "$last_license_sha" == '""' ]] && last_license_sha=""
  [[ "$series" == "null" || "$series" == '""' ]] && series=""
  [[ "$license_path" == "null" || "$license_path" == '""' ]] && license_path=""

  # Frozen entries: upstream renamed the skill away or deleted it, but we
  # keep shipping the last vendored copy. Skip fetching entirely so a
  # vanished upstream path can't break `make sync`. See `frozen:` in vendor.yaml.
  local frozen frozen_reason
  frozen=$(yq ".skills[$idx] | has(\"frozen\")" "$VENDOR_YAML")
  if [[ "$frozen" == "true" ]]; then
    frozen_reason=$(skill_field "$idx" "frozen.reason")
    [[ "$frozen_reason" == "null" ]] && frozen_reason="upstream removed"
    echo -e "$name ($owner/$repo)... ${YELLOW}frozen${NC} — skipping ($frozen_reason)"
    return 0
  fi

  echo -n "Checking $name ($owner/$repo)... "

  local latest_commit latest_license_sha=""
  latest_commit=$(get_latest_commit "$owner" "$repo" "$branch" "$path")

  if [[ -z "$latest_commit" ]]; then
    echo -e "${RED}failed to fetch latest commit${NC}"
    return 1
  fi

  if [[ -n "$license_path" ]]; then
    latest_license_sha=$(get_file_sha "$owner" "$repo" "$branch" "$license_path")
    if [[ -z "$latest_license_sha" ]]; then
      echo -e "${RED}failed to fetch license: $license_path${NC}"
      return 1
    fi
  fi

  if [[ "$latest_commit" == "$last_commit" && "$latest_license_sha" == "$last_license_sha" ]]; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}up to date${NC}"
    return 0
  fi

  if [[ "$check_only" == "true" ]]; then
    echo -e "${YELLOW}update available${NC} (${last_commit:0:7}${last_commit:+..}${latest_commit:0:7})"
    return 0
  fi

  echo -e "${YELLOW}syncing...${NC}"

  local dest
  if [[ -n "$series" ]]; then
    dest="$VENDOR_DIR/$series/$name"
  else
    dest="$VENDOR_DIR/$name"
  fi
  # Clean existing and re-download
  rm -rf "$dest"
  download_tree "$owner" "$repo" "$branch" "$path" "$dest"
  if [[ -n "$license_path" ]]; then
    download_file "$owner" "$repo" "$branch" "$license_path" "$dest/LICENSE.txt"
  fi

  # Update vendor.yaml with sync info
  local sync_date
  sync_date=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
  yq -i ".skills[$idx].last_sync.date = \"$sync_date\" | .skills[$idx].last_sync.commit = \"$latest_commit\"" "$VENDOR_YAML"
  if [[ -n "$license_path" ]]; then
    yq -i ".skills[$idx].last_sync.license_sha = \"$latest_license_sha\"" "$VENDOR_YAML"
  else
    yq -i "del(.skills[$idx].last_sync.license_sha)" "$VENDOR_YAML"
  fi

  echo -e "  ${GREEN}synced${NC} to ${latest_commit:0:7}"
}

main() {
  local check_only=false
  local filter_name=""

  while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
      --check) check_only=true; shift ;;
      -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
      -*) echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2; usage; exit 1 ;;
      *) filter_name="$1"; shift ;;
    esac
  done

  check_deps

  if [[ ! -f "$VENDOR_YAML" ]]; then
    echo -e "${RED}Error: $VENDOR_YAML not found${NC}" >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  local count
  count=$(skill_count)

  if [[ "$count" -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "No skills configured in vendor.yaml"
    exit 0
  fi

  local found=false
  for ((i = 0; i < count; i++)); do
    local name
    name=$(skill_field "$i" "name")
    if [[ -n "$filter_name" && "$name" != "$filter_name" ]]; then
      continue
    fi
    found=true
    sync_skill "$i" "$check_only"
  done

  if [[ "$found" == "false" ]]; then
    echo -e "${RED}Error: Skill '$filter_name' not found in vendor.yaml${NC}" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

main "$@"

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-08-28 08:10:31Z)**_

看完了。三個問題分開回答：

## 1. `make sync` 現在做什麼

`make sync` → `scripts/sync-vendor.sh`：對 `vendor.yaml` 每個 entry 比對上游最新 commit SHA，有差就 `rm -rf` 該 vendored 目錄重新下載，並回寫 `last_sync.date` / `commit` / `license_sha`。

**它只改工作目錄，不會 commit、不會 push。** 另外兩個對自動化有影響的行為：

- `make sync-check` 就算偵測到更新也**永遠 exit 0**（`sync_skill` 在 check 模式印完 `update available` 就 `return 0`）→ 純通知型 workflow 沒有可用的失敗訊號，要嘛加 `--exit-code`，要嘛改用 `git status --porcelain` 判斷。
- 上游把 skill 改名/刪掉時 `download_tree` 找不到檔案會 **exit 1**，整個 `make sync` 硬失敗。這其實是好事：那種情況本來就需要人來決定 `renamed_from:` 還是 `frozen:`（CLAUDE.md 已寫死這個規約）。

## 2. 定期 sync 的 GitHub Action — 可行，但我建議開 PR 而不是直接 commit main

技術上都可行（runner 有 `gh`，`GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` 讀 public repo 足夠，`yq` 補裝一下）。但直接 auto-commit 到 main 有三個實際問題：

1. **供應鏈**：vendored 內容會直接進到下游使用者的 agent context。上游被投毒或改壞，無人 review 就 push 到 main，`npx skills update` 當天就散出去。
2. **閘門會被繞過**：`make validate` 目前靠 pre-push hook（本地）和 validate.yml（CI）。bot 直推 main 不跑 hook；而且 frontmatter 壞掉時 `npx skills add` 是**靜默跳過**（你自己的 pitfall 檔就寫了這件事），錯誤不會自己冒出來。
3. **rename 判斷**：上游改名時需要人決定 `renamed_from:` + `git mv` + 改 `marketplace.json`，這不是機器能自動做的。

建議形狀：weekly cron + `workflow_dispatch` → `make sync` → 有 diff 就跑 `make validate` → `gh pr create` 到固定分支 `chore/vendor-sync`（固定分支 = 每週更新同一個 PR，不會堆一疊）。用 `gh` 自己做、不引入第三方 action，跟 repo 現有依賴一致。

⚠️ 有個必知的坑：**`GITHUB_TOKEN` 建立的 PR 不會觸發其他 workflow**，所以 validate.yml 不會在那個 PR 上跑 —— 必須在 sync job 內部就跑 `make validate`（或改用 PAT）。另外 repo Settings → Actions → Workflow permissions 要開 read/write + allow creating PRs。

## 3. Justfile — 值得，但要當成一次刻意的遷移

現在的 Makefile 是 100% phony target，本質就是 task runner 而非 build system，`just` 更貼。最大的實際收益是**變參**：

```bash
# 現在
make add-todo ARGS="--priority P3 --effort M --title 'X' --description 'Y'"
make add-vendor SOURCE=owner/repo/path
# just
just add-todo --priority P3 --effort M --title 'X' --description 'Y'
just add-vendor owner/repo/path
```

`add-todo` / `promote-todo` / `sweep-inbox` / `add-vendor` 四個都在受這個引號地獄的苦。再加上 `just --list` 自帶說明、`sync`/`test-skill` 可以吃 optional positional（腳本本來就支援單一 skill 過濾，Makefile 現在沒暴露）、`[confirm]` 可以保護 `docs-deploy`。而且你自己的 `python-project-best-practice` skill 就是推 Justfile，算 dogfooding。

成本我量過了：扣掉 `.specstory/history/` 和 `.claude/plans/`（歷史記錄，**不該改**），實際活躍的 `make <target>` 引用約 **100 處** —— CLAUDE.md 18、README 9、docs 雙語約 60、validate.yml 4、pre-push hook 和兩個 script 各幾處。不算大但也不是順手改。折衷做法是留一個 5 行 Makefile 轉發到 `just`，文件分批換。

---

兩個決定要你拍板：

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-08-28 08:20:15Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**定期 vendor sync 的 workflow 要做成哪一種？**

Options:
- **開 PR（推薦）** - weekly cron + 手動觸發 → make sync → 有 diff 就跑 make validate → gh pr create 到固定分支 chore/vendor-sync。你 review 後 merge。上游改名導致 sync 失敗時 job 紅燈通知。
- **直接 commit + push main** - 偵測到更新就自動 commit 推 main。最省事，但沒有 review 關卡，vendored 內容會直接流向下游 npx skills update。
- **只通知不改檔** - 跑 make sync-check，有更新就開/更新一個 GitHub Issue。需要先修 sync-vendor.sh 的 --check 讓它有可用的 exit code。實際 sync 仍由你本地執行。

**Justfile 要怎麼處理？**

Options:
- **遷移 + Makefile shim（推薦）** - 寫 Justfile 承接全部 target、改善變參介面，保留薄 Makefile 轉發到 just 讓 make sync 等舊指令仍可用；CI 加 setup-just；文件分批更新。
- **完整遷移，砍掉 Makefile** - 一次改完 Justfile + CI + pre-push hook + ~100 處雙語文件引用。乾淨但 diff 大，且要求所有人裝 just。
- **先記 TODO 不動** - 用 add-todo.sh 記一條 P3 項目（含上面的成本評估），這輪只做 sync workflow。
- **維持 Makefile** - make 到處都有、零安裝成本，變參的引號問題就忍著。不做這件事。


**Answer:** 開 PR（推薦）, 先記 TODO 不動

Usage: check-commit-msg.sh [OPTIONS] ["<message>"]
       printf 'feat: add x\n' | check-commit-msg.sh
       check-commit-msg.sh --agentic --staged --file .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG

Validate `<type>[(scope)][!]: <subject>`. Default mode checks the header only.

  --staged             Cross-check transcript/plan trailers against the index.
                       Requires --agentic and must run inside the target repo.
  --allow-no-body      Agentic escape hatch for a genuinely trivial commit.
  --types              Print the allowed commit types and exit.
  --help, -h           Show this help and exit.

Agentic messages reject CJK/Hangul in the human-written header/body. Tool-native
metadata (Generated-with, Co-Authored-By, cryptographic signatures) is allowed;

Output (stdout): one JSON object describing the validation result.

Exit codes:

EOF

<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>
Write vendor-sync workflow

````bash
cat > .github/workflows/vendor-sync.yml <<'YAML'
name: Vendor Sync

# Weekly `make sync` against every upstream in vendor.yaml, opened as a PR
# rather than pushed to main.
#
# Why a PR and not an auto-commit:
#   1. Vendored SKILL.md content lands directly in downstream agents' context
#      via `npx skills update` — an upstream change deserves a human diff.
#   2. A SKILL.md whose frontmatter stops parsing is SILENTLY skipped by
#      `npx skills add` (it still exits 0) — see
#      pitfalls/skill-description-colon-breaks-yaml-frontmatter.md.
#   3. When upstream renames or deletes a skill, `make sync` fails hard. That
#      needs a human to pick `renamed_from:` vs `frozen:` (see CLAUDE.md).
#
# GOTCHA: PRs created with GITHUB_TOKEN do NOT trigger other workflows, so
# validate.yml will not run on the sync PR. That is why this job runs the
# publish gates itself before handing the PR over.

on:
  schedule:
    # Mondays 03:00 UTC.
    - cron: '0 3 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      skill:
        description: 'Sync only this skill (vendor.yaml name); blank = all'
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: vendor-sync
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  SYNC_BRANCH: chore/vendor-sync

jobs:
  sync:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Pinned to the version used locally. sync-vendor.sh rewrites vendor.yaml
      # with `yq -i`, and a different yq major/minor can reflow unrelated lines
      # into the diff.
      - name: Install pinned yq
        run: |
          sudo curl -fsSL -o /usr/local/bin/yq \
            https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v4.53.2/yq_linux_amd64
          sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq
          yq --version

      - name: Sync vendored skills
        id: sync
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          ./scripts/sync-vendor.sh ${{ inputs.skill }} 2>&1 | tee /tmp/sync.log

      - name: Detect changes
        id: changed
        run: |
          if [[ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]]; then
            echo "any=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            git --no-pager diff --stat | tail -40
          else
            echo "any=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "No upstream changes."
          fi

      # Same parser `npx skills` uses, so CI agrees with the CLI rather than
      # with whatever yq the runner image ships. Mirrors validate.yml.
      - name: Install the js yaml parser
        if: steps.changed.outputs.any == 'true'
        run: npm install --no-save --no-package-lock yaml@2

      - name: Install the pinned native plugin CLIs
        if: steps.changed.outputs.any == 'true'
        run: |
          npm install --global --no-audit --no-fund @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.235
          npm install --global --no-audit --no-fund @openai/codex@0.147.0

      # continue-on-error so a broken upstream still produces a reviewable PR;
      # the job is failed explicitly in the last step.
      - name: Run publish gates
        id: validate
        if: steps.changed.outputs.any == 'true'
        continue-on-error: true
        run: |
          NODE_PATH="$PWD/node_modules" ./scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh --parser node skills
          ./scripts/validate-marketplace.sh
          ./scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only
          make native-marketplace-smoke

      - name: Open or update the sync PR
        if: steps.changed.outputs.any == 'true'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          synced=$(grep -c 'synced to' /tmp/sync.log || true)
          gates="✅ passed"
          [[ "${{ steps.validate.outcome }}" == "failure" ]] && gates="❌ FAILED — see the run log before merging"

          {
            echo "Automated \`make sync\` of \`vendor.yaml\` upstreams."
            echo
            echo "**Publish gates:** $gates"
            echo
            echo '<details><summary>sync log</summary>'
            echo
            echo '```'
            sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' /tmp/sync.log
            echo '```'
            echo
            echo '</details>'
            echo
            echo "> validate.yml does not run on this PR: GitHub does not trigger"
            echo "> workflows for PRs created with \`GITHUB_TOKEN\`. The gates above"
            echo "> ran inside the Vendor Sync job instead."
          } > /tmp/pr-body.md

          git config user.name  'github-actions[bot]'
          git config user.email '41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'

          # The sync branch is bot-owned and regenerated from main every run, so
          # a plain force push is the intended behaviour, not a lost update.
          git checkout -B "$SYNC_BRANCH"
          git add -A
          git commit -m "chore(vendor): sync ${synced} skill(s) from upstream" -F - <<EOF
chore(vendor): sync ${synced} skill(s) from upstream

Opened by .github/workflows/vendor-sync.yml. Review the vendored diff before
merging: this content ships to downstream agents via \`npx skills update\`.
EOF
          git push --force origin "$SYNC_BRANCH"

          pr=$(gh pr list --head "$SYNC_BRANCH" --state open --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')
          if [[ -n "$pr" ]]; then
            gh pr edit "$pr" --body-file /tmp/pr-body.md
            echo "Updated PR #$pr"
          else
            gh pr create --base main --head "$SYNC_BRANCH" \
              --title "chore(vendor): sync vendored skills from upstream" \
              --body-file /tmp/pr-body.md
          fi

      - name: Fail if the publish gates failed
        if: steps.validate.outcome == 'failure'
        run: |
          echo "::error::Publish gates failed on the synced vendor content — PR opened but not safe to merge as-is."
          exit 1
YAML
echo written

做完了。兩件事都落地：

## 新增 `.github/workflows/vendor-sync.yml`

每週一 03:00 UTC + `workflow_dispatch`（可帶 optional 的單一 skill filter，`sync-vendor.sh` 本來就支援但 Makefile 沒暴露）。流程：

`make sync` → `git status --porcelain` 判斷有無 diff → 有才裝 parser/CLI 並跑閘門 → 在固定分支 `chore/vendor-sync` 開/更新 PR → 閘門失敗時最後一步顯式 `exit 1`（PR 還是會開，讓你看得到 diff）。

實作上處理掉的幾個坑：

- **yq 釘死 v4.53.2**（跟你本機同版）。`sync-vendor.sh` 用 `yq -i` 回寫 `vendor.yaml`，runner 自帶的版本不同會把無關行重新排版、汙染 diff。
- **閘門在 sync job 內部跑**，不是靠 validate.yml —— `GITHUB_TOKEN` 建的 PR 不觸發其他 workflow。PR 內文會註明這件事，並附上結果與 sync log。
- **ANSI 剝除**：log 裡是 `\e[0;32msynced\e[0m to <sha>`，直接 `grep 'synced to'` 會抓不到，先 `sed` 掉再數。
- `workflow_dispatch` 的 input 走 `env:` 傳入，不直接內插進 shell（避免 injection）。
- `git add -A` 安全：`node_modules/` 已在 `.gitignore`，兩支 smoke script 都在 `mktemp` + `trap cleanup` 的隔離 `HOME` 裡跑，不會往 repo 寫東西。

⚠️ **要你手動設定一次**：Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions 設成 *Read and write*，並勾 *Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests*。沒開的話 push 分支和 `gh pr create` 都會 403。

## Justfile → TODO P3

用 `add-todo.sh` 記進 `## P3`，含我實測的成本數字（~100 處活躍引用，`.specstory/history` 和 `.claude/plans` 排除在外不該改）和遷移方案（Justfile + 薄 Makefile 轉發 + CI 加 setup-just + 文件分批）。

## 順手更新的文件

`CLAUDE.md` 的 Vendor System 段、`docs/workflows/adding-vendor-skills.md` 與 `.zh-TW.md` 各加一節「Scheduled sync」。`make validate` 三個閘門全過（66 個 SKILL.md、64 條 marketplace path、TODO 格式）。

One skill covers both directions: scaffold a new project, or score and modernize an existing one. It delegates rather than restates - verifiable-surfaces owns CLI surface design, marimo-batch-mlflow owns dual-mode notebooks, fastapi-ai-* owns FastAPI internals, and cli-release-distribution explicitly excludes Python, which is the hole this fills with uv tool install and Trusted Publishing.

The audit has no --fix: migrating a real project is a sequence of reviewable changes, and one commit doing layout, packaging, lint, and CI at once cannot be bisected.

The generated project gates its own agent docs. scripts/sync_agent_docs.py regenerates the CLI block in AGENTS.md and .agents/skills/ from --help, and just check runs it with --check, so a flag rename that skips the docs fails the build instead of silently misleading the next agent.

Three claims changed under verification rather than being written from memory:

- tyro already ships shell completion via --tyro-write-completion; the shtab wiring the plan called for is redundant, and --tyro-print-completion is deprecated because a stray print() corrupts the output.
- uv sync does not rebuild a PyO3 extension after a rust/ edit. It sees the package as installed, does nothing, and you keep running the stale binary - including debug prints just added to diagnose it. Confirmed by experiment; uv sync --reinstall-package is the fix.
- ty cannot see a compiled module, so the rust profile failed its own gate until a hand-written _rust.pyi was added.

All six profiles were generated and run before shipping: uv sync then just check (ruff format, ruff lint, ty, pytest, docs-drift) green on each, coverage 89-100%, and uv tool install to run to uninstall exercised end to end. docs(agent-history-hygiene): scope formatters past the artifact dirs

Committing transcripts puts them in reach of every tool that rewrites files in place, not just the secret scanners the skill already handles. Since ruff 0.16, ruff format formats Python inside Markdown code blocks, so it reformats .specstory/history/*.md - falsifying a record whose whole value is being verbatim, and never converging because SpecStory rewrites the same file as the session continues. Installed skills under .agents/skills/ are vendored code and equally out of a formatter's scope.

The failure is version-gated, so it ambushes on upgrade: a repo pinned to ruff>=0.15,<0.16 is clean and goes red the day someone widens the constraint. Excluding .agents alone is also not enough, because .claude/skills/<name> symlinks into it and reaches the same files by another path.

fix(agent-history-hygiene): stop shipping detect-private-key bait

Installing this skill made downstream repos unable to commit anything: pre-commit's detect-private-key flagged the skill's own tests, README, and PEM fixture under .agents/skills/. That hook matches ten byte substrings and honours no allowlist - not gitleaks:allow, not .github/secret_scanning.yml - so the consumer had no marker they could add to suppress it. Since npx skills add materialises the whole directory into their scan scope, the fix is to keep the bytes out rather than widen their exclude.

Tests now assemble key headers at runtime (pem_header/pem_block in conftest), fixtures carry __SYNTHETIC_PEM_*__ placeholders that both staging helpers expand, and prose breaks the substring. test_shipped_file_hygiene.py enforces this over the whole skill root and additionally asserts the redactor scrubs all ten BLACKLIST entries convergently.

Two related holes closed along the way. Adjacent string literals protect only the source: CPython folds them, so PuTTY/OpenVPN headers and a whsec_ shape reappeared in __pycache__/*.pyc. Splitting at the version digit and naming the fill length defeats the fold, and the OpenVPN regex now uses \d, which is also more correct. A compiled-bytecode test guards it.

The template's exclude becomes a commented stopgap pointing at npx skills update, since a fresh install no longer needs it.

# git-workflow

One consistent, opinionated git workflow that scales from a solo weekend
project to a multi-person, multi-month repo — so you (and your agents) stop
improvising commit messages, branch names, and release habits per project.
The defaults here favor a **clean, linear, reviewable history**.

Surfaces, separated by the question they answer:

| Surface | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| `references/project-tiers.md` | "Do I commit to `main`, use a `dev` branch, or open PRs?" |
| `references/conventional-commits.md` | "What exactly goes in the commit message, including AI provenance?" |
| `references/worktrees-parallel-agents.md` | "How do I run parallel agents without collisions?" |
| `references/versioning-and-releases.md` | "When and how do I tag a version?" |
| `references/branch-hygiene.md` | "Which local branches are done vs still in-dev?" |
| `scripts/branch-status.sh` | Same, as data — classify every local branch. |
| `scripts/check-commit-msg.sh` | "Is this commit message valid?" |
| `references/lazygit-cheatsheet.md` | "How do I do this in lazygit?" (learning aid) |

## Core principles

1. **Commit messages are English and follow Conventional Commits**, even when
   the prompt/conversation is in Chinese. Code history is read by tooling
   (changelogs, SemVer bumps) and future collaborators; a mixed-language log
   is harder to grep and automate. Prompts stay whatever language you like.
2. **Prefer a linear history.** Default to `pull --rebase` and fast-forward
   merges; reserve merge commits and squashes for PR integration points. A
   linear log makes `git bisect`, `git revert`, and blame legible.
3. **One logical change = one commit; one workflow phase = one commit.** For
   multi-phase / `/workflows` work, commit at each phase boundary so you can
   roll back or resume cleanly if interrupted. Don't batch unrelated changes.
4. **Never leak secrets into history.** Secret scanning + agent-transcript
   handling is owned by the [`agent-history-hygiene`](../agent-history-hygiene/SKILL.md)
   skill — this skill *defers* to it at commit/merge time rather than
```

# Project tiers — main vs dev vs PR

Read this when deciding whether to commit straight to `main`, introduce a
`dev` branch, or move to a PR-based flow — or when a project outgrows its
current tier. The goal is to match ceremony to real collaboration needs, not
to a project's ambitions.

## Table of contents

1. [The promotion signal](#the-promotion-signal)
2. [Tier 1 — solo / early](#tier-1--solo--early)
3. [Tier 2 — prod/dev split](#tier-2--proddev-split)
4. [Tier 3 — team / grown vibe-coding](#tier-3--team--grown-vibe-coding)
5. [GitHub Flow in one screen](#github-flow-in-one-screen)
6. [Choosing a merge strategy](#choosing-a-merge-strategy)

---

## The promotion signal

Don't adopt a heavier tier until the signal actually appears. Over-branching a
solo repo just adds friction; under-branching a shared repo causes collisions
and un-reviewable history.

| Move to | When |
|---|---|
| Tier 2 | someone (a deploy, a teammate, "prod") depends on a stable line while you keep working |
| Tier 3 | a second contributor appears, **or** you want a per-feature review/CI gate even solo |

You can also **skip** tiers: a solo vibe-coding project with heavy CI may go
straight to Tier 3, using PRs purely as a "ship a feature" boundary.

## Tier 1 — solo / early

One `main`. Commit directly; keep history linear.

```bash
git config pull.rebase true
git config merge.ff only

# work, commit in logical/phase-sized chunks
git add -p && git commit            # uses your commit.template

# stay current without merge commits
git pull --rebase

# optional short-lived branch, landed with no merge commit
git switch -c fix/typo
# ...commit...
git switch main && git merge --ff-only fix/typo && git branch -d fix/typo
```

Tag releases when a state is worth returning to (see
[`versioning-and-releases.md`](versioning-and-releases.md)).

## Tier 2 — prod/dev split

`main` = last released/deployed state; `dev` = integration line. Feature
branches cut from `dev`, land on `dev`, and `dev` fast-forwards to `main` at a
release boundary.

```bash
git switch dev && git pull --rebase
git switch -c feat/import-csv        # branch off dev
# ...commits...
git switch dev && git merge --ff-only feat/import-csv

# release: promote dev to main
git switch main && git merge --ff-only dev
git tag -a v0.4.0 -m "release: v0.4.0" && git push --follow-tags
```

ci(vendor-sync): open the weekly vendor sync as a PR

`make sync` rewrites skills/vendor/ and stamps vendor.yaml but never commits,
so keeping vendored skills current was a manual chore nobody scheduled. This
runs it Mondays 03:00 UTC (plus workflow_dispatch with an optional single-skill
filter, which sync-vendor.sh already supported and the Makefile never exposed).

It opens a PR on the fixed branch chore/vendor-sync instead of pushing to main.
Vendored SKILL.md content reaches downstream agents' context directly through
`npx skills update`, and a SKILL.md whose frontmatter stops parsing is silently
skipped by `npx skills add` rather than erroring - an unreviewed auto-commit
would ship both an unread upstream diff and an invisible breakage.

validate.yml does not run on that PR: GitHub does not trigger workflows for PRs
created with GITHUB_TOKEN. The sync job therefore runs the publish gates itself
(frontmatter lint with the same js yaml parser the CLI uses, marketplace, TODO
kanban, both native marketplace smokes) and reports the outcome in the PR body.
The gate step is continue-on-error so a broken upstream still produces a
reviewable PR; a final step fails the job explicitly.

Three details that would otherwise bite:

- yq is pinned to v4.53.2, the version used locally. sync-vendor.sh rewrites
  vendor.yaml with `yq -i`, and a different yq reflows unrelated lines into
  the diff.
- sync-vendor.sh colorizes unconditionally, so the success marker on disk is
  "\e[0;32msynced\e[0m to <sha>" and a plain `grep -c 'synced to'` counts zero.
  ANSI is stripped once, then reused for both the count and the PR body.
- The workflow_dispatch input is passed through env rather than interpolated
  into the script body.

A red job is the intended signal for an upstream rename or removal: sync fails
hard when upstream.path no longer resolves, and that needs a human to choose
`renamed_from:` vs `frozen:`.

Requires Settings -> Actions -> General -> Workflow permissions set to read and
write with PR creation allowed.

Also files the Makefile-to-Justfile migration as P3 with its measured cost
(~100 live `make <target>` references; .specstory/history and .claude/plans are
historical records and stay untouched), rather than doing it in this commit.
